deployment_prerequisites.name: Windows App Runtime
deployment_prerequisites.reason: The current unpackaged shell uses framework-dependent Windows App SDK deployment.

deployment_prerequisites.name: Microsoft Raw Image Extension
deployment_prerequisites.reason: Optional since 2026-08-25. Negaflow now redistributes LibRaw as libraw.dll, so DNG and camera RAW import without it. When the extension is installed its WIC codec is still tried first and LibRaw is only the fallback. Negaflow does not redistribute the extension's binary.

third_party_runtime_dependencies.name: Microsoft.WindowsAppSDK.Runtime
third_party_runtime_dependencies.current_payload: framework declaration and bootstrap support; Windows App Runtime remains an installer prerequisite

third_party_runtime_dependencies.name: Microsoft.WindowsAppSDK.Foundation
third_party_runtime_dependencies.current_payload: Windows App SDK projections and bootstrap binaries

third_party_runtime_dependencies.name: Microsoft.Web.WebView2
third_party_runtime_dependencies.exclusion: The RemoveUnusedWebView2Payload target in src/Shell/Negaflow.Shell.csproj drops Microsoft.Web.WebView2.Core.dll, Microsoft.Web.WebView2.Core.Projection.dll and WebView2Loader.dll from the copied output on x64 and ARM64. The shell renders no web content. See docs/decisions/0022-webview2-payload-boundary.md.
third_party_runtime_dependencies.notice_requirement: Not currently applicable because no WebView2 binary is shipped. If the payload is reintroduced, reproduce LICENSE.txt and NOTICE.txt with the binary distribution.

third_party_runtime_dependencies.name: Microsoft.Data.Sqlite.Core
third_party_runtime_dependencies.selection_note: The convenience Microsoft.Data.Sqlite package is deliberately not used. It floors the native SQLite at SQLitePCLRaw.lib.e_sqlite3 2.1.11, which is affected by CVE-2025-6965 (GHSA-2m69-gcr7-jv3q, CVSS 7.2) with no patched 2.x release, and restore fails NU1903 under this repository's TreatWarningsAsErrors setting. See docs/decisions/0025-managed-sqlite-catalog-provider.md.

third_party_runtime_dependencies.name: SourceGear.sqlite3
third_party_runtime_dependencies.upstream_license: SQLite itself is public domain; the Apache-2.0 terms cover SourceGear's packaging of the build.
third_party_runtime_dependencies.payload_note: First third-party native binary in the distribution. The native imaging engine still links nothing third-party, but the product payload is no longer third-party free.
third_party_runtime_dependencies.exclusion: The package carries native binaries for around 30 runtime identifiers. The RestrictRuntimeTargetsToWindows target in Directory.Build.targets keeps only win-x64 and win-arm64 in the build output, dropping roughly 48 MB of Android, iOS, Linux and WebAssembly binaries that this product cannot execute. Measured on 2026-08-07: 53,571,344 bytes across 30 runtime identifiers before, 3,788,288 bytes across 2 after.

third_party_runtime_dependencies.name: LibRaw
third_party_runtime_dependencies.license_source: LICENSE.LGPL and LICENSE.CDDL inside the pinned source archive
third_party_runtime_dependencies.payload_note: Second third-party native binary in the distribution, and the first one negaflow builds itself. Loaded at run time with LoadLibraryExW/GetProcAddress, so it is absent from the native engine's import table and the product runs without it. Windows ships no camera RAW codec (the WIC built-ins are BMP, GIF, ICO, JPEG, JPEG XR, PNG, TIFF, HD Photo, DDS); RAW otherwise needs Microsoft's Raw Image Extension from the Store, which is not preinstalled. macOS has RAW inside ImageIO, so without this the same file opens on macOS and fails on Windows.
third_party_runtime_dependencies.obligations: LGPL-2.1 requires the licence text, the complete corresponding source (or a written offer), and the ability to relink. scripts/build-libraw.ps1 stages LICENSE.LGPL, LICENSE.CDDL, COPYRIGHT, Changelog.txt and the pinned source archive into its redistributable/ directory; shipping as a separate replaceable DLL satisfies relinking.
third_party_runtime_dependencies.exclusion: Optional LibRaw dependencies (RawSpeed, Adobe DNG SDK, LCMS, libjpeg) are all left off, so libraw.dll introduces no further third-party code.
